title: Apology of Socrates
author: Xenophon

sections.heading: Xenophon's Apology of Socrates
paragraphs: The English text here is Otis Johnson Todd's Loeb Classical Library translation, verbatim ("Xenophon in Seven Volumes", vol. 4, Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press; London: William Heinemann Ltd., 1923). Nothing is modernised, paraphrased or silently corrected.

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: E. C. Marchant, ed., Xenophontis Opera Omnia, vol. 2 (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1921), an Oxford Classical Text - Greek title "Ἀπολογία Σωκράτους". The Loeb English translation used here is by Otis Johnson Todd (vol. 4, 1923).

Structure: section only (no chapter or book level). This edition carries 34 section(s) total in this witness. (Perseus/CTS's own English work-title metadata reads "Apology"; this app uses the more familiar "Apology of Socrates".)

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0032.tlg005.perseus-eng2.xml (CTS urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0032.tlg005.perseus-eng2) from the Perseus Digital Library / OpenGreekAndLatin canonical-greekLit repository. It was fetched once (cached at scripts/import-xenophon/raw/) and is bundled with the app; nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs: The importer walks the flat sequence of section <div>s directly (this work's source has NO chapter wrapper at all - confirmed by its own <refsDecl>/<citeStructure>, which declares a single "section" citation unit). Each section becomes a leaf Division (`sec-N`) with exactly one Passage.

Only transport/editorial scaffolding is removed: entities are decoded, whitespace collapsed, and Unicode normalised to NFC (a no-op for every one of these 14 source files - independently verified 0 code points remapped). markers (always redundant with an immediately-following

start) are dropped as zero-width. Editorial supplements () and corrections (, standalone or the printed half of a / pair) ARE part of what this edition prints as its running text and are kept verbatim; text the editor brackets as suspected spurious or an interpolation () is likewise KEPT, wrapped in square brackets exactly as a critical edition prints editor-bracketed text - NOT excluded (only the unemended half of a pair, and any translator footnote nested inside a , are ever excluded); all logged individually in anomalies.json, full span verbatim. Translator/editorial footnotes (, up to ~1450 in one file) and inline source-attribution labels for embedded quotations (, e.g. "Theognis") are excluded entirely as apparatus, not Xenophon's own words, and counted.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation is by Section alone (e.g. "Apology of Socrates 1"), Xenophon's and this edition's own numbering; the source carries no chapter level at all. Division.ref and Passage.ref are null throughout: this source carries no finer, page-marker-style citation scheme.

sections.heading: Known gaps & anomalies
paragraphs: Completeness. All 34 sections of this edition are present and in order.
7 translator/editorial footnote(s) (<note>) were excluded entirely as apparatus - never Xenophon's own words.

10 inline source-attribution label(s) (<bibl>, e.g. naming the poet a quoted line traces to) were excluded from the reading text as editorial apparatus - confirmed by direct inspection to be glued onto the surrounding text with no separating whitespace, i.e. never part of Xenophon's own sentence.
